evidence_excerpts: A strict order is a relation that is transitive, irreflexive, and asymmetric; the source argues that grounding lacks all three features.
claims.text: Grounding is not a strict order because it is neither transitive, irreflexive, nor asymmetric.

evidence_excerpts: The relation between truthmaker and truth is compared with member-set, part-whole, and cruel-action/wrong-action relations as initially plausible grounding cases.
claims.text: Truthmaking is a species of grounding because the relation between a truthmaker and what is true is analogous to standard ground-grounded relations.

evidence_excerpts: Whenever an entity is a truthmaker of a proposition, that entity is the alethic-fact ground of the fact that the proposition is true.
claims.text: Alethic-fact grounding is a species of grounding in which a truthmaker grounds the fact that the truthmade proposition is true.

evidence_excerpts: The source says Schaffer's support for the set case treats counterfactual necessity as sufficient in one step and necessary in another, while determinable-determinate and disjunctive cases undermine that test.
claims.text: Schaffer's set-based counterexample does not establish grounding non-transitivity because it relies on an unstable counterfactual-necessity test.

evidence_excerpts: (1) The fact that Socrates is white makes <Socrates is white> true. (2) <Socrates is white> makes <There are propositions> true. Transitivity would yield (3), but the source rejects (3).
claims.text: Truthmaking is non-transitive: Socrates' being white truthmakes the proposition that Socrates is white, and that proposition truthmakes that there are propositions, but Socrates' being white does not truthmake that there are propositions.

evidence_excerpts: Truthmaker theory is said to be committed to propositions of the form <e exists> being made true by e; if proposition A exists, it is made true by itself.
claims.text: Truthmaking is non-irreflexive because a proposition of the form <e exists> is made true by e, so an existing proposition can make true its own existence claim.

evidence_excerpts: If proposition B is true, the fact that B is true is grounded in the fact stated by B; where B says that B is true, the fact grounds itself.
claims.text: Alethic-fact grounding is non-irreflexive because if proposition B is true and says that B is true, the fact that B is true grounds itself.

evidence_excerpts: For C = <D exists> and D = <C exists>, D truthmakes C and C truthmakes D; for E = <F is true> and F = <E is true>, their truth-facts ground each other.
claims.text: Truthmaking and alethic-fact grounding are non-asymmetric because distinct propositions can mutually truthmake or ground each other's truth facts.

evidence_excerpts: Bottomless or dense grounding chains are used to argue that x can ground y without x being closer to a fundamental entity than y.
claims.text: Grounding does not entail being more fundamental than, so appeals to relative fundamentality do not rule out reflexive or symmetric grounding.

evidence_excerpts: The fact that B is true rather than not true grounds itself, and E-is-true-rather-than-not-true and F-is-true-rather-than-not-true ground each other.
claims.text: Schaffer's contrastive or differential formulation of grounding still fails to make grounding a strict order because the same examples violate differential irreflexivity and differential asymmetry.

evidence_items.excerpt: Truthmaking is presented as the relation between a true proposition and what makes it true, and alethic-fact grounding as the relation in which a truthmaker grounds the fact that the proposition it truthmakes is true.
evidence_items.overview: This formal setup matters because the paper's conclusion about grounding depends on treating truthmaking and alethic-fact grounding as cases of the broader grounding relation. If either species lacks a strict-order feature, grounding as the genus cannot be a strict order in that respect.
evidence_items.title: Truthmaking Grounds Truth Facts

evidence_items.excerpt: In the set S = {a, b, c} case, Schaffer treats c's membership as relevant to S having exactly three members, but the source argues that counterfactual necessity cannot consistently explain both the three-member and finite-member steps.
evidence_items.overview: The passage undercuts an existing non-transitivity argument before presenting the paper's own. It shows that Schaffer's case depends on shifting from counterfactual necessity as a support for grounding to counterfactual necessity as a bar against grounding, while determinable-determinate and disjunctive grounding cases resist that shift.
evidence_items.title: Schaffer Test Inconsistency

evidence_items.excerpt: (1) The fact that Socrates is white makes <Socrates is white> true. (2) <Socrates is white> makes <There are propositions> true. Transitivity would give that Socrates' being white makes <There are propositions> true, but that final claim is rejected.
evidence_items.overview: This is the paper's central proof-style counterexample to truthmaking transitivity. It preserves two plausible truthmaking links while denying the composed link, because the existence of propositions, not Socrates' whiteness, is what explains why there are propositions.
evidence_items.title: Socrates Proposition Chain

evidence_items.excerpt: Truthmaker theory is committed to a proposition of the form <e exists> being made true by e; similarly, if proposition B is true and states that B is true, the fact that B is true is grounded in itself.
evidence_items.overview: The reflexivity evidence is not an empirical observation but a pair of formal constructions. It establishes that truthmaking and alethic-fact grounding can relate something to itself, which directly violates the irreflexivity required for strict orderhood.
evidence_items.title: Self-Truthmaker Argument

evidence_items.excerpt: Let C = <D exists> and D = <C exists>; D truthmakes C and C truthmakes D. Let E = <F is true> and F = <E is true>; the fact that E is true grounds the fact that F is true, and conversely.
evidence_items.overview: These paired constructions supply non-reflexive failures of asymmetry. They matter because asymmetry is not defeated only by self-grounding; the source also claims there can be distinct relata standing in grounding-like relations in both directions.
evidence_items.title: Mutual Proposition Grounding

evidence_items.excerpt: Schaffer's contrastive grounding is formulated with facts F rather than F* grounding facts G rather than G*, but B's truth rather than falsity grounds itself, and E's and F's truth contrasts ground each other.
evidence_items.overview: The final formal check prevents a retreat to contrastive grounding from restoring strict orderhood. Even when grounding is modeled as a quaternary relation between differences, the same reflexive and symmetric constructions violate differential irreflexivity and differential asymmetry.
evidence_items.title: Differential Grounding Failure

relations.rationale: If truthmaking is a grounding species, its non-transitivity bears on grounding's strict-order status.
If alethic-fact grounding is a grounding species, its formal failures bear on grounding itself.
The truthmaking chain supplies the source's positive case against transitivity.
Self-truthmaking supplies a case against irreflexivity.
Mutual truthmaking and truth-fact grounding supply cases against asymmetry.
The contrastive-grounding reply fails to preserve strict orderhood.

source.display_title: Grounding Is Not a Strict Order

sections.body: The source's central thesis is that grounding is not a strict order. Since strict orders are transitive, irreflexive, and asymmetric, the paper aims to defeat each formal feature rather than merely challenge one controversial assumption about grounding.
sections.heading: Core Thesis

sections.body: The argument depends on classifying truthmaking and alethic-fact grounding as cases of grounding. Truthmaking connects what is true with that in virtue of which it is true; alethic-fact grounding connects a truthmaker with the fact that the truthmade proposition is true.
sections.heading: Species Strategy

sections.body: The paper distinguishes its own argument from Schaffer's. Schaffer's set example is rejected as inconclusive, while the Socrates/proposition chain is used to show that two plausible truthmaking links need not compose into a third truthmaking link.
sections.heading: Transitivity Argument

sections.body: Against irreflexivity, the paper relies on formal constructions involving existence and truth. If proposition A exists, then <A exists> can be made true by A itself; if B says that B is true, then the fact that B is true can ground itself.
sections.heading: Reflexivity Cases

sections.body: The asymmetry challenge is stronger than mere self-grounding. The source constructs distinct propositions C and D that truthmake one another's existence claims, and distinct propositions E and F whose truth facts ground one another.
sections.heading: Asymmetry Cases

sections.body: The paper anticipates the objection that grounding must be asymmetric because grounds are more fundamental than what they ground. It replies that grounding need not entail relative fundamentality, especially in bottomless or dense grounding chains without an ungrounded first element.
sections.heading: Fundamentality Objection

sections.body: A contrastive or differential version of grounding also fails to restore strict orderhood. The same self-truth and mutual-truth examples can be reformulated as differences that violate differential irreflexivity and differential asymmetry.
sections.heading: Contrastive Grounding

source_dossier.summary_long: This source is a sustained metaphysical argument against the influential assumption that grounding is a strict order. It begins from the standard definition of a strict order as transitive, irreflexive, and asymmetric, then argues that grounding lacks all three features. The strategy is indirect but systematic: truthmaking and alethic-fact grounding are presented as species or cases of grounding, so formal failures in those species have consequences for the genus. Rodriguez-Pereyra first criticizes Schaffer's proposed non-transitivity cases, especially the set S = {a, b, c}, because the argument appears to rely on an unstable counterfactual-necessity test. The paper then offers its own non-transitivity case for truthmaking: Socrates' being white makes the proposition that Socrates is white true, and that proposition can make true the existential proposition that there are propositions, but Socrates' being white is not what makes it true that there are propositions. For irreflexivity, the paper uses self-referential existence and truth propositions: if an existing proposition is itself the entity whose existence is asserted, truthmaker theory permits self-truthmaking; if a true proposition says of itself that it is true, alethic-fact grounding permits the fact of its truth to ground itself. For asymmetry, the paper uses paired propositions that mutually truthmake or mutually ground each other's truth facts. It also answers the worry that grounding must track relative fundamentality or explanatory asymmetry, arguing that bottomless or dense grounding chains show that grounding need not always mark greater fundamentality. Finally, it argues that Schaffer's contrastive, quaternary treatment of grounding does not rescue strict orderhood, because the same self-grounding and mutual-grounding patterns violate differential irreflexivity and differential asymmetry.
source_dossier.summary_short: Gonzalo Rodriguez-Pereyra argues that grounding should not be classified as a strict order. The source challenges transitivity, irreflexivity, and asymmetry by treating truthmaking and alethic-fact grounding as species of grounding, then constructing cases in which those relations fail strict-order constraints.

summary: Gonzalo Rodriguez-Pereyra argues that grounding is not a strict order. The paper builds the case through truthmaking and alethic-fact grounding, rejects Schaffer's set-based transitivity counterexample as inconclusive, then offers formal examples against transitivity, irreflexivity, and asymmetry.
